title: Embedding profile signature and similarity‑gate: INT8/FP16 calibration cadence and validation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: We need a deterministic and auditable workflow for producing embedding model quantization profiles (INT8 and FP16 fast-paths) and automated similarity drift checks that gate profile promotion. Current calibration runs are ad-hoc and lack per-corpus signatures; production has observed rare cosine similarity regressions after profile swaps. Goal: define a calibration cadence, create a canonical signature for each quant profile, and implement a similarity‑gate (cosine distribution guard) that runs in CI and as a daily sentinel in prod. Scope: calibration harness, profile artifact format, evaluation metric suite (mean cosine, tail-drop, recall@k on representative corpora), CI similarity‑gate, daily drift sentinel job, alerting thresholds and runbook for remediation.
deliverables: Calibration harness that emits profile artifacts with stable signature metadata
Quant profile semantic versioning & S3 storage path conventions
CI similarity‑gate that compares candidate profile to baseline using seeded corpus
Daily production sentinel that computes cosine distribution deltas per customer corpus and fires alerts when thresholds exceeded
Runbook for rollback and re-calibration with playbook links
acceptance_criteria: Calibration harness produces reproducible profile JSON (+ checksum) when run on same corpus seed
Candidate INT8/FP16 profile must not reduce mean cosine similarity by > 0.008 vs baseline on each representative corpus
No more than 0.03 drop at 99th percentile of per-pair cosine differences across corpora
Recall@10 measured on eval holdout must not degrade more than 0.5 percentage points
CI pipeline rejects profile artifacts that fail similarity‑gate and prevents auto-promotion
Daily sentinel runs and creates a dashboard timeseries and PagerDuty alert when high-severity drift detected
technical_notes: Profile format: flat JSON with keys: model, backend (cuda/rocm), quant_scheme (symmetric_per_channel / affine), dtype_target (INT8/FP16), layer_anchors, scale_tables (base64-encoded floats ok), checksum (sha256) and signature fields: corpus_hash, seed, timestamp, git_ref
Calibration approach: per-channel symmetric INT8 for embedding matmuls, FP16 fast-path for attention + output linear; we keep scale anchors for token- and sequence-length-aware rescales

Calibration dataset: 5 representative corpora (web, support-tickets, product-descriptions, short-queries, long-form-docs). Each run uses deterministic RNG seed and fixed batching (batch_size=64, seq_len=256) so artifacts are reproducible
Quantization knobs: clipping percentile sweep (99.9 -> 99.99), per-layer residual scaling, and optional stochastic rounding during calibration sample pass to expose numeric sensitivity
Evaluation metrics: per-embedding cosine distribution (mean, std), delta-mean, KS-test p-value vs baseline, recall@k on labeled nearest-neighbors, and spectral-angle consistency for top-k neighbors
Guard logic: the similarity-gate first checks sample-size (min 10k pairs), then compares mean delta and p99 delta. Failing either threshold or KS p-value < 0.01 will mark the profile as rejected
Drift detection: daily job computes corpus-level rolling window (7d) of mean cosine and p99 and triggers WARNING at mean-delta >= 0.005 and CRITICAL at mean-delta >= 0.01 or p99-delta >=0.04
Storage & lineage: profile artifacts written to s3://redwood-quant-profiles/{model}/{release}/{profile_version}.json and an index file mapping profile_version -> checksum -> baseline_profile

CI implementation: a GitHub Action that downloads baseline profile for the PR's model/ref, runs 2k seeded samples through the calibration emulator, computes metrics, and posts pass/fail with numeric summary to PR and to the linear ticket
Privacy: sample corpora used in CI are synthetically generated or anonymized subsets; production sentinel uses per-customer aggregated stats (no raw embeddings persisted)

Performance tradeoffs: INT8 profile reduces token throughput latency variance and memory footprint but is slightly more sensitive to corpus-skew; we recommend default FP16 for early rollouts and INT8 for mature traffic patterns with guardrails
test_plan: Unit tests for profile serializer/deserializer and checksum verification
Determinism test: run harness 5 times on same seed -> exact checksum match
Regression tests: run similarity gate in CI with known-good and known-bad profiles to assert detect/reject behavior
Scale test: daily sentinel run on 1000 customer-corpora emulation to ensure job completes within 30m and memory < 16GB
Canary rollout: for any promoted INT8 profile, deploy to 5% of traffic with per-request tagging and shadow evaluation; require 48h with no critical alerts before 100% promotion
rollout_plan: Stage 1: implement harness & profile artifact format; land PRs and run internal calibration on canary models (ETA 1 sprint)
Stage 2: CI similarity-gate + unit tests; block merges for profile promotion until gate passes
Stage 3: daily sentinel + dashboard; run in read-only for 1 week and validate false positive rate
Stage 4: enable alerts and integrate runbook for remediation; train SRE on rollback procedure
Stage 5: apply to production models and document policy for FP16/INT8 defaults per customer tier
comments: 2026-02-16 - Maya Chen: Spiked a deterministic harness using the old calibration code. Observed non-determinism from shuffling order in dataset loader — fixed by adding explicit RNG seed and stable sorting. Checksum now stable on 3 runs.

2026-02-20 - Liam O'Connor: Added symmetric_per_channel and affine quant_scheme support. Benchmarked 4 models: int8 mean-delta ranged 0.002 - 0.012 depending on corpus. Suggest tighter thresholds for high-risk corpora.
2026-02-24 - Design review (Ana Rivas): Dashboard mockups look good. Request to surface per-customer impacted_fraction metric on the alert page. Filed DES-492 for UI work.

2026-02-28 - Security (Priya Patel): Confirmed synthetic CI corpora meet PII constraints; production sentinel will only emit aggregated metrics. No KMS changes required for profile artifacts, but recommend server-side encryption on S3.

2026-03-03 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented CI GitHub Action prototype. It posts numeric summary as a comment to PR and uploads profile artifact to a dev bucket. Next: add KS-test and p99 delta checks. Marking test coverage as P2 for now.

2026-03-04 - Maya Chen: Updated acceptance criteria to tighten mean-delta threshold to 0.008 after discussion; added recall@10 condition. Also added daily sentinel thresholds and PagerDuty integration notes.
